mean: achieved in a single step (usually: it cannot be)
lit: done with a single step, or a single kick

use.how: Almost always negated, about big goals that take time: 不是一蹴而就的, 不可能一蹴而就, 绝非一蹴而就.

near.diff: 一劳永逸 is one effort that settles a problem for good; 一蹴而就 is reaching a goal at once, and usually says you can't.

cue: A friend is upset that after a month of piano lessons she still plays badly. Remind her that real skill doesn't come in one leap.

ctx.s: 学语言不是{一蹴而就}的事，要每天坚持。
ctx.en: Learning a language isn't something you finish in one go; you have to keep at it every day.

ctx.s: 减肥哪能{一蹴而就}？你才练了三天。
ctx.en: How could losing weight happen overnight? You've only exercised for three days.

ctx.s: 市长在会上说：“改革需要时间，不可能{一蹴而就}。”
ctx.en: The mayor told the meeting: "Reform takes time; it can't be done in one stroke."

ctx.s: 你以为写小说能{一蹴而就}吗？他这本书改了整整五年。
ctx.en: Do you think a novel gets written in one go? He spent five whole years revising this one.

ctx.s: 城市的污染问题由来已久，治理也绝非{一蹴而就}。
ctx.en: The city's pollution has built up over a long time, and cleaning it up won't happen in a single step.

ctx.s: 很多年轻人创业时幻想{一蹴而就}，却低估了其中的困难。
ctx.en: Many young founders dream of instant success and underestimate how hard it is.

bad.s: 他{一蹴而就}地踢进了一个球。
bad.en: (meant: he scored with a single kick)
bad.why: It is not about kicking a ball; it is about reaching a large goal at once, and is mostly used to say this can't happen.

bad.s: 祝你考试{一蹴而就}！
bad.en: (meant: good luck passing on the first try)
bad.why: It is not a wish or a blessing; it is used, usually negated, to warn that something takes time.

mean: to press on stubbornly against all advice

story.text: Sima Qian describes Zhao Yu, a strict official under Emperor Wu of Han. When high ministers came to visit him, he never returned their calls; he cut himself off from friends and guests so that no one could ask him for favours, and simply 'stood alone and pursued his single purpose'. The phrase was then about refusing influence; today it means stubbornly ignoring everyone's advice.

use.how: Predicate, often after 不顾劝阻 or 却: 他却一意孤行. Criticises someone who acts on a decision everyone advised against.

near.diff: 固执己见 is clinging to an opinion in a discussion; 一意孤行 is going ahead and acting on it despite warnings.

cue: Everyone on the team warned the manager the plan would fail, but he pushed it through anyway and it collapsed. Describe what he did.

ctx.s: 大家都劝他别辞职，可他{一意孤行}。
ctx.en: Everyone told him not to quit, but he went ahead regardless.

ctx.s: 你要是再{一意孤行}，出了事可别怪我们没提醒你。
ctx.en: If you keep ignoring everyone, don't blame us when something goes wrong; we warned you.

ctx.s: 董事会反对扩张，总经理却{一意孤行}，公司最后亏了大钱。
ctx.en: The board opposed expanding, but the CEO insisted on his own way, and the company lost a fortune.

ctx.s: 他明知道有风险，为什么还要{一意孤行}？
ctx.en: He knew the risks, so why did he insist on going his own way?

ctx.s: 医生让他住院观察，他却{一意孤行}，第二天就去爬雪山了。
ctx.en: The doctor told him to stay in hospital, but he ignored it and went off climbing a snowy mountain the next day.

ctx.s: 历史上不少君主{一意孤行}，最终导致国家衰败。
ctx.en: Many rulers in history disregarded all counsel and in the end brought their states to ruin.

bad.s: 她{一意孤行}地学习，终于考上了大学。
bad.en: (meant: she studied single-mindedly and got into university)
bad.why: It criticises ignoring advice; it is not praise for dedication. For dedication, say she studied wholeheartedly instead.

bad.s: 他一个人{一意孤行}去旅行了。
bad.en: (meant: he went travelling on his own)
bad.why: The character for 'alone' here does not mean travelling solo; the idiom means acting against everyone's advice.

mean: full of twists and setbacks along the way
lit: one sweeping stroke, three turns of the brush

story.text: The phrase began as calligraphy advice. In a note attributed to Wang Xizhi on Lady Wei's treatise on the brush, he says that each long sweeping stroke should turn the brush three times, so the line moves instead of running flat. It was later said of writing with twists in its structure, and then of any course of events full of setbacks.
story.source: 王羲之《题卫夫人〈笔阵图〉后》

use.how: Predicate or before 的, about a process, story or relationship: 事情一波三折; 一波三折的谈判. Usually looks back on a bumpy course.

near.diff: 一帆风顺 is the opposite: everything goes smoothly from start to finish.

cue: Your flight was cancelled, the next one delayed, then your bag was lost, but you finally got there. Sum up the trip.

ctx.s: 这次搬家{一波三折}，总算搬完了。
ctx.en: This move had one hitch after another, but it's finally done.

ctx.s: 他们的恋爱{一波三折}，最后还是结了婚。
ctx.en: Their romance had plenty of ups and downs, but they got married in the end.

ctx.s: “签证办得怎么样？”“别提了，{一波三折}，到现在还没下来。”
ctx.en: "How's the visa going?" "Don't ask. Problem after problem, and it still hasn't come through."

ctx.s: 这部电影情节{一波三折}，观众一直猜不到结局。
ctx.en: The film's plot keeps twisting, and the audience can't guess the ending.

ctx.s: 经过{一波三折}的谈判，双方终于签了合同。
ctx.en: After negotiations full of twists and turns, the two sides finally signed.

ctx.s: 这个项目从立项到完成，过程可谓{一波三折}。
ctx.en: From approval to completion, this project ran into setback after setback.

bad.s: 今天海上{一波三折}，船晃得厉害。
bad.en: (meant: the sea was rough today)
bad.why: It is not about real waves; it describes a process or story full of twists and setbacks.

bad.s: 这件事很顺利，{一波三折}就办好了。
bad.en: (meant: it went smoothly and was done quickly)
bad.why: It means the opposite of smooth: many setbacks along the way.

mean: to press on while the first burst of energy lasts
lit: the first drum roll rouses the fighting spirit

story.text: When Qi attacked Lu at Changshao, Cao Gui rode with the Duke of Lu and stopped him from sounding the attack when Qi first drummed. Only after Qi had drummed three times did he let Lu drum, and Lu won. He explained: battle is a matter of courage; the first drum rouses it, the second drains it, by the third it is gone. Theirs was spent while Lu's was full.

use.how: Adverbial before the verb, often urging: 一鼓作气把活干完; 一鼓作气爬到山顶. About pushing through a task while the energy lasts.

near.diff: 一气呵成 says a piece of work was done smoothly without a break; 一鼓作气 is about seizing momentum to push through a challenge.
再接再厉 is encouragement to keep improving after a success; 一鼓作气 is about not stopping now, before the energy fades.

cue: Your team has just carried the heaviest furniture upstairs and everyone is still fired up. Urge them to finish the move now, before they tire.

ctx.s: 我们{一鼓作气}爬到了山顶。
ctx.en: We kept our momentum and climbed all the way to the top.

ctx.s: 别停下来，趁大家还有劲，{一鼓作气}把活干完！
ctx.en: Don't stop; while everyone still has the energy, let's push on and finish the job!

ctx.s: 上半场领先后，球队{一鼓作气}，又连进三球。
ctx.en: Ahead at half-time, the team kept up the pressure and scored three more in a row.

ctx.s: 已经过了科目一，为什么不{一鼓作气}把驾照考下来？
ctx.en: You've passed the first driving test, so why not keep going and get your licence now?

ctx.s: 考完第一门后，她没有休息，{一鼓作气}复习下一门。
ctx.en: After the first exam she didn't take a break but went straight on to revising for the next.

ctx.s: 战士们{一鼓作气}，攻下了山头。
ctx.en: The soldiers charged on in one surge and took the hilltop.

bad.s: 他学钢琴已经{一鼓作气}十年了。
bad.en: (meant: he has persevered with piano for ten years)
bad.why: It is about the first burst of energy, not long persistence. Years of steady effort call for a word of perseverance instead.

bad.s: 他敲鼓敲得很{一鼓作气}。
bad.en: (meant: he plays the drums energetically)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with real drumming, and it is not an adjective that can follow 'very'.

mean: a tiny fraction of a huge whole
lit: one hair out of nine oxen

story.text: Sima Qian was castrated as punishment after he spoke up for a defeated general before Emperor Wu. In a letter to his friend Ren An he explained why he had not chosen death: if he had simply been executed, it would have been like nine oxen losing a single hair, no different from the death of an ant. So he bore the disgrace in order to finish his history.

use.how: Predicate or object, usually after 只是, 不过是: 这点钱对他来说只是九牛一毛. Always measured against a large total.

near.diff: 微不足道 is trivial in itself; 九牛一毛 is small compared with a huge whole it belongs to.

cue: A billionaire gives a hundred thousand dollars to charity and the press praises him. Point out how little that is next to his fortune.

ctx.s: 这点钱对他来说只是{九牛一毛}。
ctx.en: That kind of money is nothing to him; he wouldn't even notice it.

ctx.s: 公司捐了一百万，跟它的利润比起来不过是{九牛一毛}。
ctx.en: The company gave a million, but next to its profits that's a drop in the ocean.

ctx.s: 我读过的书，和图书馆的藏书相比简直是{九牛一毛}。
ctx.en: The books I've read are a tiny fraction of what the library holds.

ctx.s: 全国浪费的粮食那么多，我们省下的虽是{九牛一毛}，但也值得做。
ctx.en: So much food is wasted nationwide; what we save is a tiny fraction, but it's still worth doing.

ctx.s: 这次涨的几块钱，跟富人的财产比只是{九牛一毛}，对穷人却是很大的负担。
ctx.en: Next to a rich person's wealth, this rise of a few yuan is a tiny fraction, but for the poor it is a heavy burden.

ctx.s: 王总一年收入几千万，请大家吃顿饭，{九牛一毛}而已。
ctx.en: Mr Wang earns tens of millions a year; treating everyone to dinner costs him next to nothing.

bad.s: 他很小气，连{九牛一毛}都不肯给。
bad.en: (meant: he's so stingy he won't give a cent)
bad.why: Confused with the idiom for a miser who won't pluck one hair. This one compares a small part with a huge whole; it does not mean 'even a little'.

bad.s: 这件事{九牛一毛}，你不用管。
bad.en: (meant: it's a trivial matter, don't bother)
bad.why: It needs a huge whole to compare against. For something unimportant in itself, call it trivial instead.

mean: flooded with mixed feelings at once

story.text: As the Western Jin collapsed into war, the young scholar Wei Jie fled south. About to cross the Yangtze, worn out and grieving, he looked at the vast water and said that seeing this boundless expanse, a hundred feelings gathered in him at once; anyone who had feelings at all, how could he put them aside? The book records his words with a slightly different second character.

use.how: Predicate for a person, often with 心中 or before 地: 他百感交集. Said at a big moment: a reunion, a farewell, a return.

near.diff: 悲喜交加 is specifically sorrow and joy together; 百感交集 is many feelings at once, too many to name.

cue: Back at the school you left decades ago, you feel joy, regret, nostalgia and sadness all at once. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 看到老家的房子，他{百感交集}。
ctx.en: Seeing his old family home, he was overcome with emotion.

ctx.s: 毕业典礼上，她{百感交集}，说不出话来。
ctx.en: At the graduation ceremony, so many feelings rushed in that she couldn't speak.

ctx.s: 二十年后再见到老师，我心里{百感交集}。
ctx.en: Seeing my teacher again after twenty years, I felt a flood of mixed emotions.

ctx.s: 接过冠军奖杯的那一刻，你是不是{百感交集}？
ctx.en: The moment you took the trophy, did all kinds of feelings hit you at once?

ctx.s: 读着女儿出国前留下的信，母亲{百感交集}。
ctx.en: Reading the letter her daughter left before going abroad, the mother was torn by many emotions.

ctx.s: 离开工作了三十年的工厂那天，老张{百感交集}地回头看了一眼。
ctx.en: The day he left the factory where he'd worked for thirty years, Lao Zhang looked back once, full of mixed emotions.

bad.s: 今天我买了新衣服，心里{百感交集}。
bad.en: (meant: I bought new clothes and I'm really happy)
bad.why: It means many mixed feelings at a moving moment, not simple happiness. Simply say you are happy.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜{百感交集}，什么口味都有。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant has every kind of flavour)
bad.why: It describes a person's emotions, never a variety of things.

lit: a thousand changes, ten thousand transformations

use.how: Predicate or before 的, about weather, clouds, situations, techniques: 天气千变万化; 千变万化的图案. Not a verb with an object.

near.diff: 瞬息万变 stresses speed: a situation or market changing from moment to moment; 千变万化 stresses the countless forms something takes.
五花八门 is many different kinds side by side; 千变万化 is one thing that keeps changing form.

cue: Watching clouds drift over a mountain, you see them become one shape after another, never the same twice. Describe them.

ctx.s: 天上的云{千变万化}，一会儿像马，一会儿像狗。
ctx.en: The clouds keep changing shape: one moment a horse, the next a dog.

ctx.s: 孙悟空会七十二变，{千变万化}，妖怪根本认不出他。
ctx.en: The Monkey King has seventy-two transformations and can take any form; the demons never recognise him.

ctx.s: 万花筒里的图案{千变万化}，孩子们看得入迷。
ctx.en: The patterns in the kaleidoscope never stop changing, and the children are spellbound.

ctx.s: 中国菜的做法{千变万化}，同一块豆腐能做出几十道菜。
ctx.en: Chinese cooking has endless variations; the same tofu can become dozens of dishes.

ctx.s: “这些都是同一个字？”“对，在书法家笔下，一个字也能写出{千变万化}的样子。”
ctx.en: "Are these all the same character?" "Yes. In a calligrapher's hand, even one character can take countless forms."

ctx.s: 你知道吗？围棋的下法{千变万化}，几乎没有两盘完全一样的棋。
ctx.en: Did you know? Go can be played in endlessly varied ways; almost no two games are ever the same.

bad.s: 他{千变万化}了自己的计划。
bad.en: (meant: he changed his plan many times)
bad.why: It is not a verb and cannot take an object; it describes something that takes ever-changing forms.

bad.s: 他是个{千变万化}的人，答应的事经常变卦。
bad.en: (meant: he's fickle and often goes back on his word)
bad.why: It neutrally describes varied forms, not an unreliable person. Fickleness needs a different word.

mean: at the critical moment, hanging by a thread
lit: a thousand jun (an old weight) hanging from a single hair

use.how: Mostly in 千钧一发之际 or 千钧一发的时刻, about a split second of real danger, often just before a rescue or escape.

near.diff: 迫在眉睫 is a task or threat that is urgently close; 千钧一发 is the split second of extreme danger itself.

cue: A child runs into the road; the driver slams the brakes and the car stops inches away. Describe that instant.

ctx.s: 就在这{千钧一发}的时刻，消防员冲了进去。
ctx.en: At that critical instant, the firefighters rushed in.

ctx.s: {千钧一发}之际，司机猛踩刹车，车停在了孩子面前。
ctx.en: At the last possible moment the driver slammed on the brakes, and the car stopped right in front of the child.

ctx.s: 火车越来越近，小狗还卡在铁轨上，情况{千钧一发}。
ctx.en: The train was getting closer and the puppy was still stuck on the tracks; everything hung by a thread.

ctx.s: 你还记得那次{千钧一发}的经历吗？我们差点掉下悬崖。
ctx.en: Do you remember that close call? We nearly went over the cliff.

ctx.s: 比赛只剩最后几秒，守门员在{千钧一发}之际扑出了点球。
ctx.en: With seconds left in the match, the goalkeeper saved the penalty at the decisive moment.

ctx.s: 回想起那{千钧一发}的一刻，他现在还觉得后怕。
ctx.en: Thinking back to that moment when everything hung by a thread, he still feels shaken.

bad.s: 这个月的房租要交了，真是{千钧一发}。
bad.en: (meant: rent is due, it's urgent)
bad.why: It is for a split second of real danger, not an ordinary deadline. Just say it is urgent.

bad.s: 他力气很大，有{千钧一发}之力。
bad.en: (meant: he has enormous strength)
bad.why: Confused with the phrase for the strength of a thousand jun. This idiom describes a moment of danger, not strength.

mean: so lifelike it seems alive (a painting, a carving)

use.how: Predicate or complement, praising a depiction: a painting, sculpture, craft or written character: 画得栩栩如生. Never about a real living thing.

near.diff: 惟妙惟肖 praises an imitation for being exactly like the original, including impersonations; 栩栩如生 says a depiction seems alive.

cue: At a museum you see an old ink painting of shrimps so real you half expect them to swim off the paper. Praise it.

ctx.s: 他捏的泥人{栩栩如生}。
ctx.en: The clay figures he makes look alive.

ctx.s: 这幅画上的马{栩栩如生}，好像要跑出来一样。
ctx.en: The horse in this painting is so lifelike it looks ready to gallop out of the frame.

ctx.s: 你看这尊木雕，是不是{栩栩如生}？
ctx.en: Look at this wood carving; doesn't it seem alive?

ctx.s: 博物馆里的兵马俑个个{栩栩如生}。
ctx.en: Every one of the terracotta warriors in the museum looks lifelike.

ctx.s: 这些糖做的小动物{栩栩如生}，孩子们都舍不得吃。
ctx.en: The little sugar animals are so lifelike the children can't bear to eat them.

ctx.s: 这部小说里的乡村老师形象{栩栩如生}，好像就生活在我们身边。
ctx.en: The village teacher in this novel is so vividly drawn he seems to live among us.

bad.s: 我奶奶九十岁了，还{栩栩如生}。
bad.en: (meant: my grandma is ninety and still full of life)
bad.why: It praises a depiction that looks alive, not a real person's vitality. Say she is still full of energy instead.

bad.s: 这首歌{栩栩如生}，我很喜欢。
bad.en: (meant: this song is lively, I love it)
bad.why: It is for visual or written depictions that seem alive; a song can be lively, but not lifelike.

lit: carriages like flowing water, horses like a dragon

story.text: When Emperor Zhang of the Eastern Han wanted to give titles to the brothers of Empress Dowager Ma, she refused. She said that passing the Zhuolong Gate she had seen the people calling on her family, their carriages like flowing water and their horses like a swimming dragon. Her family was already grand enough, she said, and she refused to add honours.

use.how: Predicate or before 的, describing a street or city scene: 街上车水马龙; 车水马龙的大街. Traffic that is busy but moving.

near.diff: 人山人海 is huge crowds of people; 车水马龙 is a lively stream of vehicles on the streets.
水泄不通 is packed so tight nothing moves; 车水马龙 is busy traffic that keeps flowing.

cue: From your hotel window downtown you watch cars and buses streaming along the avenue all evening. Describe the street.

ctx.s: 市中心的大街上{车水马龙}，非常热闹。
ctx.en: The streets downtown are busy with traffic and full of life.

ctx.s: 这里以前是一片农田，现在已经{车水马龙}了。
ctx.en: This used to be farmland; now it's busy with traffic.

ctx.s: 站在天桥上，看着下面{车水马龙}的街道，他觉得自己很渺小。
ctx.en: Standing on the footbridge, watching the stream of traffic below, he felt very small.

ctx.s: 一到晚上，酒店门口就{车水马龙}，客人来来往往。
ctx.en: Every evening, cars pull up one after another at the hotel entrance as guests come and go.

ctx.s: 离开{车水马龙}的城市，回到安静的山村，她终于睡了个好觉。
ctx.en: Leaving the busy city behind for a quiet mountain village, she finally got a good night's sleep.

ctx.s: 你住的地方{车水马龙}的，晚上不吵吗？
ctx.en: There's so much traffic where you live; isn't it noisy at night?

bad.s: 地铁里{车水马龙}，挤得我透不过气。
bad.en: (meant: the subway was so crowded I could hardly breathe)
bad.why: It describes vehicles flowing along streets, not people packed inside. For packed crowds, use the idiom about mountains and seas of people.

bad.s: 昨天高速公路上发生了{车水马龙}的事故。
bad.en: (meant: there was a multi-car crash on the motorway)
bad.why: It paints a lively, busy street scene, not a crash or disaster.
